coaching.summary: Take the bar from a rack onto your back, press it overhead on a wide grip, then squat until your hips sink below your knees and stand back up, arms locked throughout.
cues: Take a wide grip, lock the elbows, and press up into the bar before you descend.
Keep the bar stacked over mid-foot and sit straight down between the hips.
Keep pushing up into the bar and stand without letting it drift forward.

introduction.title: Why the Overhead Squat Is Worth Learning
paragraphs: The overhead squat holds a barbell at arm's length above your head on a wide grip while you squat to full depth and stand back up. It tests everything at once: shoulder stability, upper back strength, hip and ankle mobility, and the balance to keep the bar over the middle of your foot.

It is also the receiving position of the snatch, so weightlifters use it to build confidence under the bar. For everyone else it is a brilliant teacher. Any weak link in your squat shows up the moment the bar is overhead, and strengthening it improves every other squat you do.
Begin with a PVC pipe or an empty bar.

faqItems.question: How wide should my grip be for the overhead squat?
faqItems.answer: Use a snatch grip, wide enough that the bar sits in the crease of your hips when you stand with straight arms. The wider grip lowers the bar and makes the overhead position more stable for most lifters.

faqItems.question: Why does the bar fall forward in my overhead squat?
faqItems.answer: The bar drifts forward when the torso leans or the shoulders relax. Keep pushing up into the bar the whole time, keep it stacked over the middle of your foot, and sit straight down. Tight ankles and hips often cause the lean, so mobility work pays off quickly.

faqItems.question: Is the overhead squat good for beginners?
faqItems.answer: It is a great skill to practise with a PVC pipe or empty bar from day one, because it teaches strong squat positions. Heavier loading can wait until your back squat and strict press feel solid and your mobility allows full depth.

faqItems.question: What mobility do I need for the overhead squat?
faqItems.answer: Good shoulder flexion to hold your arms overhead, upper back extension to stay tall, and enough hip and ankle mobility to squat upright. Squatting with a PVC pipe and holding the bottom position for a few breaths is a simple way to build all three.
